analysis.investment_thesis: HGINFRA is a high-growth EPC contractor with strong historical revenue CAGR of 23.8% and decent ROE of 18.3%, but it fundamentally violates my most sacred rule: the balance sheet is dangerously leveraged at D/E of 1.83, with borrowings exploding 10x from ₹520 Cr in 2020 to ₹5,669 Cr in 2025. A business that has never generated positive free cash flow in recent history and is burning ₹2,415 Cr of cash annually is not a business — it is a liability in disguise.
key_strengths: Promoter holding of 71.78% is high and signals skin-in-the-game
Operating margin of 18.63% is exceptional for an EPC contractor, showing execution discipline
9-year revenue CAGR of 23.8% demonstrates strong order-book execution and industry positioning
key_risks: Debt/Equity of 1.83 is 6x my acceptable limit; borrowings surged from ₹1,513 Cr (2024) to ₹5,669 Cr (2025) in a single year — deeply alarming
Free cash flow has been negative every single year: -₹379 Cr (2022), -₹457 Cr (2023), -₹525 Cr (2024), -₹2,415 Cr (2025) — this business consumes capital, it does not generate it
Revenue and profit both declined in FY2025 (revenue -6%, net profit -6.3%) just as capex exploded to ₹1,561 Cr — high execution risk on new projects
red_flags: D/E of 1.83 — absolute dealbreaker; my hard limit is 0.3
OCF positive in only 1 of last 5 years; 2025 OCF was -₹878 Cr
Borrowings grew 10x in 5 years — entirely debt-funded growth model
CWIP jumped from ₹14 Cr to ₹1,322 Cr in one year — massive speculative capital deployment
Finance costs compounding at 36.6% CAGR, matching net profit growth — debt is eating all earnings
analysis.detailed_analysis:
I built DMart on one principle: never owe what you cannot repay from operations. HGINFRA's balance sheet is the antithesis of that philosophy. In FY2025, the company borrowed ₹4,156 Cr net (financing CF of +₹2,310 Cr) while burning ₹878 Cr from operations and ₹1,461 Cr in investments. Total debt has ballooned to ₹4,170 Cr against equity of ₹3,087 Cr. The business earns ₹505 Cr in net profit but has never once converted earnings into free cash in recent memory. That gap between accounting profit and cash reality is the oldest danger in investing.

Infrastructure EPC is also simply not my circle. These businesses live and die on government contract flows, budget cycles, and project execution risk — none of which I can predict or control. The sector demands perpetual capital recycling, which means you are always dependent on bankers and markets. A good business should generate surplus cash and return it to owners; HGINFRA does the opposite. The P/E of 10.6x looks tempting, but cheap valuations in leveraged cyclicals are often value traps. I will pass.
